Data Handling Documentation

Technical reference · September 24, 2026 · Version 2.7

This document provides a detailed technical account of how Remvoll stores and protects data, complementing the plain-language Privacy Policy. It is intended for privacy-conscious users, security reviewers, and enterprise or regulatory diligence.

1. Architecture overview

Remvoll for iOS is a local-first native application. All persistence is on the user's device: settings, presets, sleep history and any background photos in the app's sandboxed container, secrets in the iOS Keychain. There is no backend application server, no cloud database, no sync service, and no telemetry pipeline. The app ships with no third-party SDKs of any kind — no analytics, advertising, attribution, or crash-reporting libraries — and makes no network requests in normal use. All audio is synthesised on the device.

2. Encryption at rest

  • Every stored record is encrypted using AES-256 in GCM mode with a fresh, cryptographically-random 96-bit initialization vector per write, providing both confidentiality and integrity (authenticated encryption).
  • The key is a 256-bit symmetric key generated on the device on first run and stored in the iOS Keychain with accessibility kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly: it is unavailable until the device has been unlocked once after boot, and it is marked as never migrating to another device, so it is not carried into an iCloud or encrypted-iTunes backup.
  • Encrypted files are written with iOS complete file protection until first user authentication and are flagged excluded from backup, so a backup of the phone does not contain a copy of them.
  • No passwords or credentials are stored, hashed or otherwise, because the app has no accounts. There is no password verifier, no salt, no recovery code and no session token in the data model at all.

3. Data inventory

  • settings — theme, volume, breathing pace and depth, sleep timer, microphone mode, effects and haptics toggles, alarms, last mix, jet-lag plan, app-blocking schedules, wind-down reminder time, and the version of the terms you accepted. Purpose: preferences. Retained until you delete the app.
  • sleep-timing pattern — running statistics about when you fall asleep and how your sleep cycles run, folded out of Apple Health readings where you have allowed them. No samples, no per-night records. Purpose: so Smart Wake can aim for a light moment without a Watch. Retained until you erase your sleep history or delete the app.
  • presets — the sound mixes you name and save. Purpose: core feature. Retained until you delete them or the app.
  • sessions — playback summaries: start and end time, duration, sounds and intensities, breathing setting, disturbance counts. Purpose: your Sleep Score page. Retained as a rolling window of the last 400 sessions, or until Erase sleep history.
  • alarm bookkeeping (in UserDefaults, not encrypted, because it is not personal) — the mapping from our alarm identifiers to the system's, the tone each alarm uses, and per-day snooze counts. Retained until the alarm is deleted. UserDefaults also holds two dates: the last day an upgrade prompt was shown, and when the rating prompt was last offered.
  • morning note (encrypted, only if you record or type one) — a short recording made deliberately from the alarm screen, and its text where offline dictation is available. Purpose: showing you the note the next morning. Retained until you record another one, which replaces it, or until you delete it. Exactly one exists at a time.
  • app-blocking rules (in a shared App Group container, not encrypted, because the monitor extension has to be able to read them and cannot reach the encrypted store) — the schedules you create: their times, days, name and on/off state; for each rule, an OPAQUE TOKEN BLOB returned by iOS describing which apps you picked; and a record of which block is in force right now and when it ends. The token blob is not readable by us or by the app. iOS hands back sealed identifiers rather than names, so Remvoll genuinely cannot tell which apps you chose, cannot count them by name, and cannot see whether you ever opened them. Purpose: blocking apps when you asked, and lifting the block on time. Retained until you delete the rule or the app.
  • background photos (in the app container, not encrypted by Remvoll, only if you add one) — the part of a picture you framed, saved at screen size, plus a small thumbnail, a reduced copy of the whole picture (at most 3,000 pixels on its long side) and a small file recording the framing, so the photo can be re-framed later. iOS gives the app only the picture you pick, never your library. Not excluded from backups, so they are included in an iCloud or computer backup of your iPhone like other app files. Purpose: your background. Retained until you remove the photo (touch and hold it in Settings › Background) or delete the app.
  • encryption key (in the Keychain, not in the container) — used to encrypt everything above. Removed with the app.

There is no users record, no session, no credential store and no membership record, because there are no accounts and Apple holds the subscription.

4. Data flows

  • Microphone (opt-in only): device audio → an in-memory level meter → one root-mean-square loudness value every couple of seconds → either a disturbance count for your Sleep Score page or a small bounded adjustment to playback volume. The buffer is discarded immediately; audio is never recorded, encoded, persisted or sent anywhere, and the microphone is released when the mode is turned off or playback stops.
  • Screen Time / Family Controls (opt-in only): your choice of apps is made in an Apple-provided picker that returns sealed tokens rather than names, so no app identity ever reaches Remvoll. The tokens, your schedules and the currently-active block are stored in a shared App Group container so a background helper can lift a block on time. No app-usage information is read, derived, retained or transmitted, and nothing leaves the device.
  • HealthKit (opt-in only): sleep and overnight samples (heart rate, heart rate variability, breathing rate, blood oxygen, wrist temperature), as recorded by an Apple Watch or another device or app that writes to Apple Health, are read on the device to choose a moment for Smart Wake and to work out the Sleep Score. The samples are used for that night and not retained, and the Sleep Score's figures are recomputed from Health each time its page opens rather than stored. A derived statistical summary of your sleep timing IS retained on the device — see "Health readings" above for exactly what it contains and does not contain — so that Smart Wake continues to work on nights you do not wear a Watch. Access is read-only; Remvoll never writes to Health, and neither the samples nor the derived summary is ever copied off the device.
  • Notifications (opt-in only): the trial reminder and the wind-down reminder are local notifications scheduled with iOS on the device. There is no push service and no server; iOS shows them at the time given.
  • Siri and Shortcuts: Apple invokes Remvoll's "Start sleep" and "Stop" actions through the App Intents framework. The app receives the action and nothing else.
  • Exports: user-initiated. A JSON document is assembled in memory and handed to the iOS share sheet, where you choose the destination. Nothing is transmitted by the app itself.
  • Network: none in normal use. The app makes no requests, has no analytics endpoint, and contains no third-party SDK that could make one.

5. Deletion and portability

  • Settings › Export my data yields a complete, human-readable JSON copy for portability.
  • Settings › Erase sleep history clears your sleep history and the sleep-timing pattern, and leaves presets and settings alone.
  • Deleting the app removes everything: the container, every encrypted record and the Keychain key, which makes any residual ciphertext permanently undecryptable. There is no separate "delete account" step because there is no account to delete.

6. Backups, sync, and recovery

No server-side backup or synchronisation exists. The encryption key is marked "this device only", so the data is not restored by an iCloud or iTunes backup either: if the iPhone is lost or the app deleted, the data goes with it. That is a deliberate trade-off of the privacy-first design, not an oversight. Use Export to keep anything you care about. Any future optional sync would be end-to-end encrypted, opt-in, and documented here before it shipped.

7. Sub-processors

Remvoll engages no sub-processors, because no personal data leaves the device. Apple acts as the merchant of record for subscriptions and receives your payment details directly under its own terms; it receives no Remvoll data, because the app sends none. If any processor is ever introduced, it will be listed here with its role and location before it goes live.

8. Breach considerations

Because Remvoll holds no centralised store of user data, the class of risk represented by a server-side breach does not exist. The residual risk is local: access to an unlocked iPhone. Protect the device with a passcode, Face ID or Touch ID, and use the Export and Erase controls as appropriate. Should a future networked feature change this risk profile, we will maintain an incident-response process and notify affected users and regulators as required by applicable law.
